testcase.name: ../../testdata/sql/MR101/bad/basic.sql
testcase.failure: error MR101 ../../testdata/sql/MR101/bad/basic.sql:1 Index creation blocks writes on "orders" why: Postgres holds this lock until the whole index is built. INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on the table wait for the entire build. fix: Build the index concurrently, outside a transaction: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_orders_status ON orders (status);
testcase.system-out: warning MR403 ../../testdata/sql/MR101/bad/basic.sql:1 No lock_timeout before locking DDL why: If a long query holds a lock on orders, this statement waits for it, and every query that arrives afterwards queues behind this statement. fix: Set a lock timeout at the top of the migration, and retry the migration if it times out: SET lock_timeout = '5s';

warning MR201 ../../testdata/sql/MR201/bad/to_varchar.sql:1 Changing the type of "users.name" may rewrite the table why: Some changes to this type only update the catalog, such as varchar to text or a longer varchar limit. Other changes rewrite every row of users under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. migrail can't see the current column type in this migration. fix: Change the type with expand and contract instead of rewriting the table in place: Add name_new with the new type: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN name_new varchar(255); Write to both columns and backfill name_new in batches Read from name_new, then drop name and rename name_new
